label: Translated spatial Indigenous sovereignty into Anishinaabe ecological recovery
description: Inheriting Vine Deloria Jr.'s paradigm of land-centered sacred geography and tribal sovereignty, Winona LaDuke forged practical and philosophical resistance around wild rice (manoomin) protection, land buybacks, and post-carbon energy.
dialecticalTension: Grounds Indigenous metaphysical spatiality in contemporary environmental economics and law.
historicalContext: White Earth Land Recovery Project (founded 1989) & All Our Relations (1999).

citations.author: Winona LaDuke
citations.work: All Our Relations: Native Struggles for Land and Life

label: Shared Anishinaabe-Potawatomi ethics of kinship and botanical reciprocity
description: Rooted in parallel Great Lakes Anishinaabe/Potawatomi traditions, Kimmerer's "grammar of animacy" and LaDuke's seed sovereignty / Seventh Generation economics together define contemporary North American Indigenous environmental philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Pairs botanical-phenomenological reciprocity with frontline political-economic activism.
historicalContext: Contemporary Great Lakes Indigenous environmental philosophy.

citations.author: Winona LaDuke
citations.work: Recovering the Sacred: The Power of Naming and Claiming

label: Built transnational Indigenous-Global South front against biopiracy and patenting
description: LaDuke collaborated directly with Vandana Shiva in international forums against corporate patenting of staple seeds (connecting India's basmati struggles with Anishinaabe manoomin wild rice defense).
dialecticalTension: Forges solidarity between Indigenous land ethics and Global South agrarian commons.
